bindings.template: Notably, the strongest learned configuration in this stack is the current-only terminal triple at \CurrentOnlyAnswerThreeSeenRR\% Seen and \CurrentOnlyAnswerThreeUnseenRR\% Unseen, which we therefore report as the unrestricted deployment default.

Replacing each same-user intermediate target with an outcome-equivalent peer target raises coverage from \CrossUserTargetSameUserSeenRR\% to \CrossUserTargetOtherUserSeenRR\% on Seen and from \CrossUserTargetSameUserUnseenRR\% to \CrossUserTargetOtherUserUnseenRR\% on Unseen, that is, by 4.3 points [-7.71, -0.84] and 6.0 points [-11.79, -0.41] in the paired same-minus-peer direction, with exact McNemar \(p=0.005\) and \(p=0.032\)

On 181 student-held-out trajectories, terminal targets repair 155 trajectories and intermediate targets 92, a difference of 34.8 points with student-cluster interval \PairedJavaStudentRRCI and exercise-cluster interval \PairedJavaExerciseRRCI
of \PairedJavaJointRepairs joint repairs, intermediate targets retain \PairedJavaLexicalRetention more lexical-token points and \PairedJavaLineRetention more line points

Replacing greedy decoding by one stochastic draw costs 7.6 points \StochasticOneMinusGreedyOneSeenCI, whereas execution-selecting three of those identical fixed draws contributes \SameDrawThreeMinusOneSeen points \SameDrawThreeMinusOneSeenCI

Through \(T=1.0\) the one-draw rate stays within \SweepTOnePointZeroSeenSingleRR--\SweepTPointTwoSeenSingleRR\% on Seen, the three-draw union reaches \SweepTOnePointZeroSeenRR/\SweepTOnePointZeroUnseenRR\%, and at \(T=1.5\) the decoder collapses to \SweepTOnePointFiveSeenRR/\SweepTOnePointFiveUnseenRR\%

Fine-tuning contributes a second, larger effect: the matched base-model three-draw union reaches only \BaseStochasticThreeSeenRR/\BaseStochasticThreeUnseenRR\%, so adaptation adds \AnswerStochasticMinusBaseSeen points \AnswerStochasticMinusBaseSeenCI on Seen and \AnswerStochasticMinusBaseUnseen points \AnswerStochasticMinusBaseUnseenCI on Unseen.

At matched temperature, replacing three draws of one checkpoint by one draw from each of three checkpoints changes RR by \(-0.1\) points \CheckpointStochasticMinusSameCheckpointSeenCI on Seen and \CheckpointStochasticMinusSameCheckpointUnseen points \CheckpointStochasticMinusSameCheckpointUnseenCI on Unseen

A current-only four-cell comparison on a single inference stack agrees: three greedy checkpoints gain \FactorialGreedyThreeMinusOneSeen \FactorialGreedyThreeMinusOneSeenCI and \FactorialGreedyThreeMinusOneUnseen \FactorialGreedyThreeMinusOneUnseenCI points over one, but under the matched stochastic decoder distinct checkpoints add only \FactorialDistinctMinusSameSeen points \FactorialDistinctMinusSameSeenCI and \FactorialDistinctMinusSameUnseen points \FactorialDistinctMinusSameUnseenCI

Absolute greedy-three coverage is \FactorialGreedyThreeSeenRR/\FactorialGreedyThreeUnseenRR\% on that stack against \CurrentOnlyAnswerThreeSeenRR/\CurrentOnlyAnswerThreeUnseenRR\% on the historical one, so stack sensitivity is material and no backend-independent deployment advantage follows.
the primary five-fold cross-fitted mixed-minus-terminal contrast is \(+2.2\) points \CrossFitMixedMinusAnswerNineSeenCI and the non-cross-fitted estimate \(+1.7\) [-0.79, 4.29]

at the portfolio level, removing history instead improves frozen mixed and terminal RR by \PromptFrozenMixedCurrentMinusFullSeen/\PromptFrozenAnswerNineCurrentMinusFullSeen Seen points and \PromptFrozenMixedCurrentMinusFullUnseen/\PromptFrozenAnswerNineCurrentMinusFullUnseen Unseen points, with all intervals excluding zero

Because trajectory availability rather than randomized difficulty defines the split, the higher absolute rate does not mean that unseen problems are easier: a pre-repair audit that matches all 54 Unseen problems to distinct Seen problems on six outcome-free difficulty covariates turns the raw gap into \(-4.6\) problem-balanced points \DifficultyMatchedUnseenMinusSeenCI, which is why we rely on within-split paired contrasts.
repeating the procedure on all 328 Seen problems with a distinct seed yields \SeenHiddenMixedHiddenConfirmation\% and \SeenHiddenAnswerNineHiddenConfirmation\% confirmation

The conventional endpoint is also not load-bearing: across 2,770 Seen and 674 Unseen executable prefixes of eventually successful trajectories, the deployed configuration reaches \AllPrefixSeenRR\% and \AllPrefixUnseenRR\% RR, and the early, middle, and last thirds reach \AllPrefixEarlySeenRR\%, \AllPrefixMiddleSeenRR\%, and \AllPrefixLastSeenRR\% on Seen and \AllPrefixEarlyUnseenRR\%, \AllPrefixMiddleUnseenRR\%, and \AllPrefixLastUnseenRR\% on Unseen.
At 1.5B parameters three checkpoints still gain \ScaleAnswerThreeMinusOneSeen points over one \ScaleAnswerThreeMinusOneSeenCI, but mixed-minus-terminal is \(-0.8\) \ScaleMixedMinusAnswerNineSeenCI

on Java the same contrast is positive on four held-out exercises (\CodeWorkoutProblemMixedMinusAnswerNine points \CodeWorkoutProblemMixedMinusAnswerNineCI) and inconclusive on held-out students (0.6 [-1.20, 2.59])

The exercise estimate rests on four clusters only: refitting with one exercise left out keeps the contrast between \ExerciseSensitivityLOOMinimum and \ExerciseSensitivityLOOMaximum points, and single exercises range from \ExerciseSensitivityPerMinimum to \ExerciseSensitivityPerMaximum points

Models retrained on them agree with the canonical ones on \VerdictOrderStrictAgreementSeen\% and \VerdictOrderProgressAgreementSeen\% of Seen repair decisions (Section~\ref{sec:generality}), so we read the ranking as operational rather than universal.
retraining both relations under the binary verdict order changes intermediate-target RR by \VerdictOrderProgressCanonicalMinusAlternativeSeen and \(-2.8\) points

Exact matches between a returned repair and a training-time accepted program occur in \SeenOverlapMixedExactRate\% and \SeenOverlapAnswerNineExactRate\% of selections, near-duplicates above a 0.90 token-similarity threshold in \SeenOverlapMixedNearNinetyRate\% and \SeenOverlapAnswerNineNearNinetyRate\%, and the median maximum similarity to any same-problem training target is \SeenOverlapMixedMedianSimilarity\% and \SeenOverlapAnswerNineMedianSimilarity\%, so non-exact reuse is bounded rather than excluded
